subject: Clarify SOC 2 report scope & point-in-time exceptions
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmebio.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: SOC2 coverage dates and point-in-time evidence

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our vendor risk assessment and need to confirm a couple of items about Redwood's SOC 2 Type II. Can you confirm the audit period covered by the most recent report (start and end dates) and whether the end month (Jan 2026) is inclusive?

Additionally, we have a few point-in-time questions: for control tests that rely on snapshots (change management, access reviews), what date(s) were used as the point-in-time evidence?

Finally, if there were any changes to production configuration after the report period, is Redwood able to provide a bridge letter or attestation covering a short gap? If so, what is the typical turnaround and what dates can you cover?

Appreciate the quick clarification — our security team (cc'd at soc@acmebio.com) needs this for the procurement file.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Security Analyst
Acme BioTech

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmebio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 13:50:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage dates and point-in-time evidence

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below, and Monica (our Head of Compliance) is looped in for any technical evidence details.

1) Audit period: the attached SOC 2 Type II report covers the period July 1, 2025 through January 31, 2026 (both dates inclusive).

2) Point-in-time evidence: most control testing was performed across the period, but specific tests that are point-in-time (for example, the change-management test and one user-access snapshot) used evidence dated January 15, 2026.

3) Bridge letter: yes, we can provide a bridge letter to cover changes after the report end date for a limited timeframe. We typically issue a bridge letter that attests to no material control changes between the report end date and the letter date. Lead time is normally 3-5 business days once we have the exact target date and scope; we can cover up to 30 days post-report end as a standard practice, longer by exception.

Attached is the report excerpt and a draft bridge-letter template for your auditor to review. If Crowe (cc'd) needs a specific phrasing, we can adapt.

Next step: can you confirm the exact date you need coverage through (for the bridge letter) and whether your review requires the point-in-time evidence to be the same as the snapshot date we used?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Platforms
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmebio.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage dates and point-in-time evidence

Thanks Vivek — that helps. A couple follow-ups from our auditor:

- Can you confirm that January 31, 2026 is fully inclusive for control operation (i.e., controls in place throughout that day), and that no scheduled maintenance or planned production configuration changes occurred on that date that would affect the tests?
- Our auditor also asked whether the January 15 snapshot was a full-system snapshot or limited to specific components (web tier vs infra).
- For the bridge letter, we might need coverage through Feb 28, 2026. Is that within the standard 30-day window you mentioned? If not, would Redwood consider a focused attestation for that 28-day gap?

If you can put Monica or your audit contact in touch with Crowe directly that would speed things up.

Best,
Jordan

---
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmebio.com>, Crowe Audit <audits@crowe.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage dates and point-in-time evidence

Jordan / Crowe team — thanks for the follow-ups. A few clarifications from our compliance evidence notes: 

• Inclusivity of Jan 31, 2026: the report's control population is inclusive of January 31st. There were no scheduled production configuration rollouts that day that would invalidate operation of controls used in testing. Routine maintenance windows are scheduled (and documented) but did not occur on 1/31.

• Snapshot scope (Jan 15, 2026): the point-in-time evidence referenced in the report relates to a full production configuration snapshot for all customer-facing services and the underlying compute/storage configurations used in our control tests. It excludes isolated dev/test environments; we can provide the snapshot manifest if Crowe wants the file-level listing.

• Bridge letter covering through Feb 28, 2026: that is 28 days after the report end date (1/31) and within our standard 30-day window. We can provide a bridge letter that attests to no material changes affecting the control objectives between 1/31/2026 and 2/28/2026. Turnaround: we can deliver a signed bridge letter within 4 business days after we confirm the exact language with Crowe.

Action items: 
- Crowe: if you have specific phrasing or additional evidence requirements, please reply to this thread or send a short requirements doc.
- Jordan: I'll upload the snapshot manifest to the drive link and share an access-only view.

Monica Patel
Head of Compliance
